title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is section III ('Le groupe M_{ρ,σ}') of the notes on the 'équation des lacets'. The previous page treated the 'cas complet modulaire', with elliptic points ρ (order 3) and σ (order 2) and Borel-type subgroups of GL(2,Ẑ). This page brings in the moduli of elliptic curves.

(1) The geometric group 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} is the profinite completion of the orbifold fundamental group of the j-line with branch orders (2,3,∞), i.e. PSL(2,Z)^ ≅ (Z/2 * Z/3)^. The extended version 𝔊^∧_{0,3} includes orientation reversal, ≅ PGL(2,Z)^. Diagram (1) displays two central extensions by {±1}:
- SL → 𝔊^{+∧}, i.e. SL(2,Z)^ → PSL(2,Z)^;
- GL → 𝔊^∧, i.e. GL(2,Z)^ → PGL(2,Z)^.
Their quotients are compatible via det, giving {±1} → {±1}. Profinite completion is exact here because ±1 is finite and central.

(2) M^~_{0,3} is the arithmetic group: an extension of Γ_Q (Gal(Q̄/Q)) by 𝔊^∧_{0,3}, i.e. the arithmetic orbifold fundamental group of the 'rigidified' modular curve. It has a canonical homomorphism to GL(2,Ẑ)' = PGL(2,Ẑ) (cf. §45): this is the action on the Tate module of an elliptic curve, defined only up to sign.

N^~_{1,1} is defined as the pull-back of the central extension 1→{±1}→GL(2,Ẑ)→GL(2,Ẑ)/±1→1 along this map. Diagram (3) is the resulting morphism of exact sequences 1→{±1}→N^~_{1,1}→M^~_{0,3}→1. In modern terms, N^~_{1,1} = π_1(M_{1,1}⊗Q), the arithmetic fundamental group of the moduli stack of elliptic curves. The μ_2-gerbe M_{1,1} → M_{1,1}^{rig} is recovered from the projective Tate-module representation, because the generic automorphism −1 acts as −1 on the Tate module.

Marginal remark: 𝔗_{1,1} ≅ GL(2,Z), the extended mapping class group of the once-punctured torus.

The last line starts to identify the inverse image of the geometric part 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} ⊂ M^~_{0,3} in N^~_{1,1} with SL(2,Z)^ (resp. GL(2,Z)^ for the extended version). The next page states this explicitly: 1→SL(2,Z)^→N^~_{1,1}→Γ_Q→1, mapping onto 1→SL(2,Ẑ)→GL(2,Ẑ)→Ẑ^*→1 with the cyclotomic character, followed by a semidirect splitting M^~_{0,3} ≅ M^~_{0,3}(0)·𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3}.

Correctness of the pull-back construction: any extension of M^~_{0,3} by central ±1 that maps ±1 isomorphically onto ±1 ⊂ GL(2,Ẑ) is canonically the pull-back. So the definition agrees with π_1 of the stack.
errors: In diagram (1) the groups are written Sl(2,Ẑ) and Gl(2,Ẑ) (hat on Z), but if 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} denotes the profinite completion PSL(2,Z)^ (as the next page, which uses Sl(2,Z)^ = T^{+∧}_{1,1}, indicates), the middle terms should be Sl(2,Z)^ and Gl(2,Z)^. These are not GL(2,Ẑ), since the congruence subgroup property fails for SL(2,Z). This is either a slip carried over from the congruence ('𝔊 = Sl(2,Ẑ)') setting of the previous page, or a transcription ambiguity. The page's own first line says 'Gl(2,Z)^'.
Minor: the final sentence is unfinished, and the notation N_{1,1} versus N^~_{1,1} is used inconsistently.

ideas.what: Arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1} over Q obtained as the pull-back of GL(2,Ẑ)→PGL(2,Ẑ) along the projective Tate-module representation of the arithmetic π_1 of the (2,3,∞) orbifold j-line
ideas.modern_name: π_1(M_{1,1,Q}) as a central μ_2-extension of π_1 of the rigidified stack; gerbe class pulled back from GL_2→PGL_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; arithmetic π_1 of M_{1,1} studied by Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto, Hain–Matsumoto (1990s–2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the modular tower and M_{1,1}, but not this explicit pull-back construction as far as I know

ideas.what: Extended mapping class group of the once-punctured torus ≅ GL(2,Z); orientation-preserving part ≅ SL(2,Z)
Short exact sequence 1→SL(2,Z)^→π_1(M_{1,1,Q})→Γ_Q→1 mapping to 1→SL(2,Ẑ)→GL(2,Ẑ)→Ẑ^*→1 via the Tate module and the cyclotomic character (on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy exact sequence for M_{1,1}; monodromy representation on the Tate module

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct, but standard construction of the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1} as a ±1 central extension of the (2,3,∞)-orbifold group via the projective Tate module. It is well known in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller / anabelian literature; nothing here appears absent from that literature.
transcription_corrections: Top line: 'Considérons l'extension Gl(2,Z)^ de 𝔊^{±∧}_{0,3} par {±1}' — the superscript on 𝔊 looks like '±∧' rather than '+∧', with dashed arrows down to the diagram.
'On s'intéresse au ... N^~_{1,1}': the illegible word is probably 'groupe'. The insertion reads 'extension de M^~_{0,3} par {±1}' and the bracket reads '(image inverse de l'extension'.
Last line: 'd'induction' is more likely 'induisant'. The line reads roughly '... l'image inverse de 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} ⊂ M^~_{0,3} dans N_{1,1}, ..., Gl(2,Z)^, induisant'.
In (3), a crossed-out 'M_{0,3}' precedes {±1}, and the vertical isomorphism marks under GL(2,Ẑ) and GL(2,Ẑ)' are '≀' (possibly meaning 'not iso' or wavy arrows).
